key_insight: Low DFT energy and force errors do not guarantee reliable disordered-carbon simulations; MACE-MH-1 was the most consistently robust foundation MLIP tested.
engineering_relevance: Foundation MLIPs can support nanoporous-carbon modelling, but realistic O/H-containing systems require application-specific stability and structural validation.
method: Screen six foundation MLIPs using DFT energy and force errors and binding curves.
Run melt-quench-anneal molecular dynamics with four models.
Evaluate structural observables across pure and O/H-containing disordered carbons.
evidence_signal: All four MD-tested models reproduced principal experimental and specialised-potential signatures of nanoporous carbon, while binding curves and O/H-containing trajectories exposed failures missed by low DFT errors.
watch_item: Shared structural biases among OMAT-based models suggest that training coverage can limit reliability despite architectural differences.
paper_title: Challenging Atomistic Foundation Models on Disordered Carbons
